title: Container With Most Water
statement: You are given an integer array height of length n. Picture n vertical lines where line i goes from (i, 0) to (i, height[i]). Choose two lines that, together with the x-axis, form a container holding the most water. Return the maximum amount of water the container can store. The container cannot be tilted.

examples.explanation: Lines at index 1 (height 8) and index 8 (height 7) give min(8,7) * (8-1) = 49.

keyInsights: Start with the widest container (pointers at both ends)
Area is limited by the shorter line, so always move the pointer at the shorter line inward; moving the taller one can never help
referenceSolution:
def maxArea(height):
    l, r, best = 0, len(height) - 1, 0
    while l < r:
        best = max(best, min(height[l], height[r]) * (r - l))
        if height[l] < height[r]: l += 1
        else: r -= 1
    return best
hintLadder: Try computing the answer by hand for height = [1,8,6,2,5,4,8,3,7]. Which pair wins, and why?
Start with the widest possible container. If you shrink the width, what has to happen for the area to get bigger?
Keep one pointer at each end and always move the pointer at the shorter line inward, tracking the best area so far.
